model_identifier: claude-sonnet-5 (analyst reasoning over blind_inputs, not an automated pipeline call)

dimensions.evidence_used: 'genuinely large, thesis-compelling long-term market opportunity (transportation electrification)'
dimensions.rationale: Real, large, explicit market thesis.
No category-growth-rate data for the nascent EV category at this snapshot.
No named trigger event distinct from the general electrification thesis (Market Size's domain).

dimensions.evidence_used: 'essentially no successful independent new automaker precedent in the U.S. in the prior several decades'
dimensions.rationale: Real, explicit, direct negative evidence about category difficulty -- a stated historical failure-base-rate, not mere absence.
Real paying customers exist (Roadster deposits) but that is realized Traction evidence, which must not be reused here.

dimensions.evidence_used: Musk described as having taken an 'increasingly central operational role... having been an early investor and chairman'
dimensions.rationale: No explicit prior automotive-industry operating background stated -- role is described as investor-turned-operator, not domain-veteran.

dimensions.evidence_used: 'successfully designed and begun shipping a genuine, working product... a real, non-trivial engineering achievement'
dimensions.rationale: Strong, explicit, real shipped-complexity evidence -- a working car, not a prototype.
No commercial-leadership-background specifics.

dimensions.evidence_used: 18% workforce reduction (69 of 384 employees) during the November 2008 cash crisis
dimensions.rationale: Real, direct evidence of organizational distress at this snapshot's lead-up, though such cuts are also a defensible crisis-response action -- genuinely mixed-leaning-negative.

dimensions.evidence_used: shipped a genuine, working product (Roadster) despite near-bankruptcy
dimensions.rationale: A real, mixed-but-net-positive execution signal: a hard technical milestone achieved despite severe financial adversity.

dimensions.evidence_used: customers 'pre-paid substantial deposits' for the Roadster
dimensions.rationale: Real, direct willingness-to-pay evidence -- customers pre-paid for an unproven-at-scale product.

dimensions.evidence_used: 'a functioning, shipping, high-performance electric sports car'
dimensions.rationale: Real, named, category-defining differentiation -- electric and high-performance was a genuinely novel combination at this time.
No onboarding/ownership-experience evidence stated; the concept applies differently to a physical product but no evidence exists either way.

dimensions.evidence_used: Daimler battery/electric-drivetrain collaboration announced alongside the investment
dimensions.rationale: Real evidence of an emerging technical-partnership-based capability advantage, though not yet a proven durable moat.
No named adjacent-market/segment expansion surface at this single-product, single-segment snapshot.
No CAC/pipeline/sales-motion evidence (direct-sale luxury car, no GTM-process data given).

dimensions.evidence_used: shipped Roadster alongside a real 18% workforce reduction
dimensions.rationale: Real shipped product, but under severe resource constraint -- net-neutral, genuinely mixed evidence.

dimensions.evidence_used: documented near-bankruptcy: ~$9M cash remaining, 18% workforce reduction, last-minute financing close on Christmas Eve 2008
dimensions.rationale: Direct, severe, real, well-sourced negative operational evidence -- not absence, a documented crisis.

dimensions.evidence_used: Daimler strategic partnership specifically targeting a battery/drivetrain capability gap
dimensions.rationale: A real, sound strategic choice, made under financial duress but addressing a genuine capability need.
Deposits mentioned generically, no unit-count figure.
No revenue data.
No retention evidence.
Physical, one-time-purchase product; no telemetry-based engagement concept applies the same way as a software product.
No growth series.
No revenue data.
No margin/CAC data; the previously-included Roadster price figure was removed during evidence repair as unverifiable and is not used here.

dimensions.evidence_used: the near-bankruptcy episode itself: severe cash depletion, workforce cuts, last-minute financing
dimensions.rationale: This is the single most severe, best-evidenced financial-distress case in the whole portfolio, yet it still cannot produce a Burn Efficiency number under the Deterministic architecture -- the burn-multiple formula requires revenue-relative inputs a pre-revenue-at-scale hardware company in crisis does not have. Flagged as an important PASS A finding: the architecture cannot represent this company's most decision-relevant fact.

dimensions.evidence_used: ~$9M cash on hand (Nov 2008), a real, dated cash-position figure
dimensions.rationale: Unlike most other companies in this portfolio (total evidence absence), Tesla has a real cash-position number -- the specific gap is the missing burn-rate figure needed to convert cash-on-hand into a months-of-runway score against the FROZEN linear bands (18mo/24mo/<6mo). This is a cleaner, more specific gap than total absence, distinguished explicitly as a partial-input case.
